challengeAdjudicated.challenge: FIX13 refused Motion items 2 and 3 and recorded that the refusal was beyond its assignment, for an independent lane to challenge rather than inherit. VF13 had previously failed the family for, among other things, item 2 swearing a conviction before 25 June 2019 on fixtures whose printed arrest dates are 2021 and 2023.
challengeAdjudicated.reasoning: I confirm from the bytes that items 1.a, 1.b, 2 and 3 now carry no tick by either mechanism, and that the refusal is correct on four independent grounds. (1) The platform holds no conviction date and no sentence-completion proof; both are sworn statements on a motion the movant signs, and asserting either would fabricate a participant fact. (2) The record itself makes proof of sentence completion a document to OBTAIN before filing, so item 3 cannot be true at build time by construction. (3) The canonical fixture's printed arrest date is 03/12/2021 and the boundary's is 11/29/2023, both after 25 June 2019, so a ticked item 2 would have printed a statement the packet's own printed data contradicts on the same page. (4) The route spans both a misdemeanour and a Class 4 felony and convictionClass is a required participant answer, so item 1's limb is not determined by the route either. All four are disclosed to the movant with the reason and the instruction to tick them from the certified disposition, and the guide adds the cross-check that a motion saying misdemeanor in item 1 and Class 4 felony in item 4 contradicts itself. Refusing these and disclosing them is the correct behaviour, not a gap.

challengesRecorded: Fixture plausibility, not scored as a counter: both fixtures depict arrests in 2021 and 2023 on a route whose item 2 requires a conviction before 25 June 2019, so neither fixture depicts a movant who is facially eligible for the relief the packet requests. The packet asserts no eligibility, so nothing false is printed, but the fixtures demonstrate rendering rather than a workable matter.
